description.narrative: Insatsens syfte är att stärka Etiopiens möjlighet att fortsätta sitt ambitiösa arbete inom social trygghet vilket inkluderar utveckling av ny policy och system samt att stärka genomförandet av stöd till utsatta grupper såsom internflyktingar och barn samt i utvecklingen av nya innovativa stödprogram. Insatsen förväntas härigenom bidra till konkreta resultat för att minska flerdimensionell fattigdom i Etiopien. Sida har valt att kanalisera ett stöd om MSEK 75 via UNICEF under 2025-2018 och till programmet Social trygghet – stärkt resiliens och försörjning.

The objective of the intervention is to strengthen Ethiopia's capacity to continue its ambitious work in social protection, including the development of new policies and systems, and to strengthen the implementation of support to vulnerable groups such as IDPs and children, as well as in the development of new innovative programmes. The intervention is expected to contribute to concrete results in reducing multidimensional poverty in Ethiopia. Sida has chosen to channel the support, MSEK 75, through UNICEF 2025-2028 to the programme “Social Protection - Strengthening Resilience and Livelihoods”.

The overall objective of the programme is:
to establish effective systems for holistic social protection to promote empowerment and resilience of the most vulnerable women and children in rural and urban Ethiopia
The specific objectives of the program are:
I. To create an enabling environment, enhance the legal frameworks and national policies and the national capacity to deliver social protection programmes,
II. To increase shock-responsiveness through enhanced coverage and effective linkages to urban and rural safety net and HCT interventions,
III. To facilitate and strengthen socio-economic inclusion through improved access to economic opportunities and skills development, for both PSNP and other social assistance recipients,
IV. To enhance service linkages through the cash plus care approach and generate evidence from interventions to enhance the effectiveness of the PSNP/UPSNJP with a particular focus on child-sensitive social protection.
The core proposed programme activities are:
- support strengthening capacity of MoWSA, its regional and respective woreda offices, to implement cash plus care and support programs to support implementation of the permanent and temporary direct support components of the rural and urban PSNP,
- support strengthening capacity of MoWSA, regional bureuas and respective woreda office for shock responsive social protection programming
- support the capacity of MoWSA for evidence-based planning, policy dialogue, formulation, revision, implementation, and monitoring of holistic, child-disability sensitive, gender transformative, financially inclusive and resilience building social protection systems.

description.narrative:
The results directly correspond to the planned outputs and indicators in the Results Based Management framework:
Direct reach and equity focus
Humanitarian Cash Transfers (HCTs): 6,516 households (27,721 individuals) reached across Amhara, Oromia and Tigray. 62% were women-headed households (exceeding the 50% target), 48% children, 40.5% IDPs, 24.6% returnees, and 795 persons with disabilities received top-ups of ETB 2,500.
Child Grant: 2,557 households (11,403 individuals) targeted and verified in Addis Ababa, Afar, Amhara, Oromia and Sidama (on track for the 2028 target of 2,500 households). 38% pregnant women, 62% with children under one 23% female headed 10% overlapping with PSNP Temporary Direct Support. Overall: 39,124 individuals supported (52.1% girls and women).
Cash Plus service linkages and behavioural change
HCT: In Amhara, 2,323 individuals (8.4% of beneficiaries) were actively linked to services (health/nutrition: 101 psychosocial: 525 CBHI enrolment: 323 child protection: 177).
Child Grant: High early uptake in several regions e.g., 100% of pregnant women in Addis Ababa and Afar received tetanus vaccination 69.5% of children under one received birth certificates 60.3% of children under one vaccinated strong rates of ANC attendance (up to 83.3% in Afar), immunization cards, and CBHI enrolment (up to 54.8% in Amhara).
Baseline surveys confirmed extreme vulnerability (98% food insecurity across HCT areas very low dietary diversity and service access), validating that interventions reached the intended most needy populations.
Accountability and inclusion mechanisms 291 Targeting and Appeals Committee members trained and operational (~39%women). Over 1,200 grievances recorded and 100% resolved through functioning Grievance Redress Mechanisms.
Capacity building and system strengthening 401 staff (38.7% women) trained on HCT and PSEA 417 staff (39.3% women) trained on disability identification >140 stakeholders trained on Child Grant delivery.
47 social workers deployed (key to last mile delivery and referrals). Embedded technical assistance: five senior advisers placed in MoWSA MIS specialist deployed to coordinate national social registry work following the World Bank diagnostic.
Unexpected Positive Results
Higher than planned gender and disability inclusion: 62% women-headed households in HCT (well above the 50% target) and proactive disability top-ups plus dedicated training for 417 staff on internationally recognized tools (Washington Group questions Child Functioning Module) indicating stronger than anticipated equity focus in targeting.
Exceptionally high grievance resolution rate (100%): This reflects highly effective, trusted Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) mechanisms and a rapid shift in community government relationships toward transparency and responsiveness an outcome that exceeded typical early stage expectations.
Early and tangible policy influence: The GESI assessment and design of the rigorous Child Grant study (1,500 households, quasi experimental, four waves) were completed on schedule and already directly informing PSNP 6 revisions and the National Social Protection Policy update. This level of evidence to policy linkage in the first reporting period is a strong early win.
Rapid institutional embedding and ownership: Full implementation through government structures (federal, regional, woreda, kebele) with high-level MoWSA buy-in, including the social registry diagnostic and preparation for the 2026 Africa Social Protection Conference, shows faster than anticipated government leadership and sustainability potential.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
